title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List
description:
You are given the `head` of a singly linked list and a 1-indexed integer `k`.

Swap the **values** of the `k`-th node from the beginning and the `k`-th node from the end of the list, and return the `head` of the list. Solve the problem in a single traversal using `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is n, with 1 <= k <= n <= 10^4.
hints: Walk a `lead` pointer `k - 1` steps from `head` to locate `first`, the `k`-th node from the start.
Then start `second` at `head` and advance `lead` and `second` together until `lead.next` is null; `second` lands on the `k`-th node from the end.

examples.explanation: The 2nd node from the start (2) and 2nd node from the end (4) swap values to produce [1, 4, 3, 2, 5].
The 5th node from the start (9) and 5th node from the end (0) swap values.
When k = 1 on a 1-node list, both pointers refer to the same node so the list is unchanged.
